concerns: Ambiguity: 'Time (ns)' is defined as whatever per-frame value the trajectory reader assigns (deterministically fixed here since the DCD stores no times), yet it is graded scientifically at 1e-9 absolute tolerance. A submission that reports true reader times is indistinguishable from one that happens to know the convention; beyond representation, the time column cannot be scientifically counterexampled without rerunning a reader, which the offline evidence does not permit.

The tolerance rule's 3e-6 A absolute floor is generous relative to the frame-0 self-comparison values (~1e-7), so near-zero self-RMSD results could plausibly be perturbed by up to a few e-6 and remain within tolerance; I deliberately probed above the floor to keep value failures unambiguous.

The acceptance rule does not explain how the reference frame-0 time of ~0.9999999119200186 ns arises (it appears to be dt*(frame+1) rather than dt*frame); the addendum asserts both accepted implementations coincide, which was not independently verifiable from the reference outputs alone.

probes.name: backbone-domain-values-bias
probes.rationale: Recomputes every Backbone/CORE/LID/NMP value in backbone_rmsd.csv as value*1.05+0.001 while keeping row count, Frame ids, Time (ns), ordering and format intact. All backbone RMSD columns then violate computation 1 (backbone RMSD of the full backbone set plus domain-group RMSDs after global fitting), but the frame/time/structure checks remain satisfied, isolating the value checks.
probes.script:
import csv
path = 'backbone_rmsd.csv'
with open(path, newline='') as fh:
    rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
assert rows[0] == ['Frame', 'Time (ns)', 'Backbone', 'CORE', 'LID', 'NMP'], rows[0]
out = [rows[0]]
for row in rows[1:]:
    assert len(row) == 6
    out.append([row[0], row[1]] + [repr(float(v) * 1.05 + 0.001) for v in row[2:]])
with open(path, 'w', newline='') as fh:
    csv.writer(fh, lineterminator='\n').writerows(out)
print('shifted %d backbone value rows' % (len(out) - 1))

probes.name: time-single-file-drift
probes.rationale: Adds a 1e-6 ns drift to the Time (ns) column of core_ca_rmsd.csv only, exceeding the 1e-9 absolute time tolerance and breaking the identical-Time-per-frame cross-file consistency while all RMSD values remain correct. This also exercises the time-tolerance boundary per frame.
probes.script:
import csv
path = 'core_ca_rmsd.csv'
with open(path, newline='') as fh:
    rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
assert rows[0] == ['Frame', 'Time (ns)', 'CORE'], rows[0]
out = [rows[0]]
for i, row in enumerate(rows[1:]):
    frame, t, core = row
    new_t = float(t) + 1e-6 * i
    out.append([frame, repr(new_t), core])
with open(path, 'w', newline='') as fh:
    csv.writer(fh, lineterminator='\n').writerows(out)
print('drifted time for %d rows' % (len(out) - 1))

probes.name: truncated-frames-lazy
probes.rationale: Truncates mass_weighted_rmsd.csv to the first 50 data frames (dropping frames 50-97) and inserts 'inf' in the last retained row to mimic a partially failed run. This violates the one-row-per-frame structural rule (missing rows rejected), and the nonfinite value additionally breaks the finite-value rule; the scientific value check on that file also fails because frames are missing.
probes.script:
path = 'mass_weighted_rmsd.csv'
with open(path) as fh:
    lines = fh.read().splitlines()
header, data = lines[0], lines[1:]
assert header == 'Frame,Time (ns),C-alphas,CORE,LID,NMP', header
assert len(data) == 98, len(data)
rows = data[:50]
parts = rows[-1].split(',')
parts[2] = 'inf'
rows[-1] = ','.join(parts)
with open(path, 'w') as fh:
    fh.write('\n'.join([header] + rows) + '\n')
print('truncated to %d rows with one inf' % len(rows))

probes.name: core-vs-backbone-cross-association
probes.rationale: Replaces core_ca_rmsd.csv's CORE column with the corresponding backbone_rmsd.csv CORE values: a different scientific quantity (core alpha-carbon RMSD after fitting that set alone onto frame 0 vs domain-backbone RMSD after a global backbone fit; they differ by ~0.02-1.55 A across the trajectory). Row count, Frame ids and Time (ns) are preserved, so this tests that the per-file scientific interpretation is checked rather than just domain plausibility.
probes.script:
import csv
bb = {}
with open('backbone_rmsd.csv', newline='') as fh:
    rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
header = rows[0]
assert header[0].strip() == 'Frame' and header[3].strip() == 'CORE', header
for row in rows[1:]:
    frame = int(float(row[0]))
    bb[frame] = float(row[3])
path = 'core_ca_rmsd.csv'
with open(path, newline='') as fh:
    rows2 = list(csv.reader(fh))
assert rows2[0] == ['Frame', 'Time (ns)', 'CORE'], rows2[0]
out = [rows2[0]]
swapped = 0
for row in rows2[1:]:
    frame = int(float(row[0]))
    if abs(bb[frame] - float(row[2])) > 1e-6:
        swapped += 1
    out.append([row[0], row[1], repr(bb[frame])])
assert swapped > 0, 'replacement must differ from reference values'
with open(path, 'w', newline='') as fh:
    csv.writer(fh, lineterminator='\n').writerows(out)
print('replaced core-ca values with backbone CORE for %d frames (%d differ)' % (len(out) - 1, swapped))

probes.name: resid-vs-mass-backbone-confusion
probes.rationale: Overwrites mass_weighted_rmsd.csv's RMSD columns with the same-frame resid_weighted_rmsd.csv values, simulating the common implementation error of using the wrong weights (resid instead of atomic mass). The two quantities differ by up to ~3.5 A late in the trajectory. Row count, Frame ids, times and headers are preserved, so only the mass-weighted scientific check should fail, plus the general value checks on that file.
probes.script:
resid = {}
with open('resid_weighted_rmsd.csv') as fh:
    lines = fh.read().splitlines()
assert lines[0] == 'Frame,Time (ns),C-alphas,CORE,LID,NMP', lines[0]
for line in lines[1:]:
    parts = line.split(',')
    resid[int(float(parts[0]))] = parts
path = 'mass_weighted_rmsd.csv'
with open(path) as fh:
    mass_lines = fh.read().splitlines()
assert mass_lines[0] == 'Frame,Time (ns),C-alphas,CORE,LID,NMP', mass_lines[0]
mass = []
for line in mass_lines[1:]:
    parts = line.split(',')
    mass.append((int(float(parts[0])), parts))
assert len(mass) == len(resid) == 98
out = [mass_lines[0]]
changed = 0
for frame, m_parts in mass:
    r_parts = resid[frame]
    assert len(m_parts) == len(r_parts) == 6
    if any(abs(float(a) - float(b)) > 1e-6 for a, b in zip(m_parts[2:], r_parts[2:])):
        changed += 1
    out.append(','.join([m_parts[0], m_parts[1]] + r_parts[2:]))
assert changed > 0, 'resid values must differ from mass values'
with open(path, 'w') as fh:
    fh.write('\n'.join(out) + '\n')
print('replaced mass-weighted RMSDs with resid-weighted RMSDs; %d/%d frames differ' % (changed, len(mass)))

probes.name: representation-full-precision-gen
probes.rationale: Client-identical representation alternative: normalizes every per-frame table to a uniform full-precision scientific-notation literal (%.17e) and rewrites Frame as an integer literal after verifying that every value parses back to the exact reference value. All value contents, row count, ordering, headers and per-frame time consistency are preserved; the spec permits fixed, scientific or shortest-round-trip notation and either '7' or '7.0' for the Frame column, so all checks should still pass.
probes.script:
import csv, math
files = {
    'backbone_rmsd.csv': ['Frame', 'Time (ns)', 'Backbone', 'CORE', 'LID', 'NMP'],
    'core_ca_rmsd.csv': ['Frame', 'Time (ns)', 'CORE'],
    'mass_weighted_rmsd.csv': ['Frame', 'Time (ns)', 'C-alphas', 'CORE', 'LID', 'NMP'],
    'resid_weighted_rmsd.csv': ['Frame', 'Time (ns)', 'C-alphas', 'CORE', 'LID', 'NMP'],
}
for path, header in files.items():
    with open(path, newline='') as fh:
        rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
    assert rows[0] == header, (path, rows[0])
    out = [rows[0]]
    for row in rows[1:]:
        assert len(row) == len(header)
        frame = int(float(row[0]))
        new = [str(frame), '%.17e' % float(row[1])]
        for v in row[2:]:
            x = float(v)
            assert math.isfinite(x) and x >= 0.0
            new.append('%.17e' % x)
        out.append(new)
    with open(path, 'w', newline='') as fh:
        csv.writer(fh, lineterminator='\n').writerows(out)
    with open(path, newline='') as fh:
        new_rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
    for a, b in zip(rows[1:], new_rows[1:]):
        assert float(a[0]) == float(b[0])
        for x, y in zip(a[1:], b[1:]):
            assert float(x) == float(y), (path, x, y)
    print('normalized %s (%d rows)' % (path, len(out) - 1))

probes.name: open-closed-representation-fixed
probes.rationale: Rewrites the single-value file from the shortest-round-trip form 6.823686867261616 to a fixed-notation literal at 17 decimal digits, which round-trips to the identical float; the spec explicitly permits fixed notation at full precision, so both the structural and value checks should still pass.
probes.script:
path = 'open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv'
with open(path) as fh:
    lines = fh.read().splitlines()
assert lines[0] == 'backbone_rmsd_angstrom', lines[0]
assert len(lines) == 2, lines
value = float(lines[1])
s = '%.17f' % value
assert float(s) == value, (s, value)
